projects.title: Merge a Brainrot
projects.role: Product owner and designer, team of two
projects.summary: A phone-first Roblox merge game I ran as product owner: 63 updates in eight days, tested with simulated players.
projects.detail:
Merge a Brainrot was a Roblox merge-and-collect game: hatch eggs, merge Brainrots, rebirth and fish for treasure. I ran it as product owner and designer from October 22 to November 3, 2026, with one teammate. I made every gameplay, pricing and release call, and AI coding agents (Claude) wrote the code to my specs.

- Oct 27 | Rebuild | We restarted on an AI-assisted build at version 29. I set the rules: phones first, every button works by touch, and no clutter on the phone screen.
- Oct 28-30 | Core loops | Eggs and hatching, merging, the shop, game passes and a map overhaul. I priced every pass and pack. The tutorial felt too long and slow, so I cut it to the core lesson and moved fishing to the boat dock.
- Oct 31 | Research | I had icon and thumbnail studies run across 32 and 495 Roblox games, and planned retention fixes once day-one numbers came in.
- Nov 2 | Retention | Players were quitting early, so I had us build simulated-player tests that play like an impatient kid. After 11 fixes, first-five-minute runs went from 0 of 24 passing to 24 of 24. I also wrote a new intro story and reworked rebirth so players keep their best Brainrot.
- Nov 3 | Last update | Version 92. Every publish passed the automated test suite and a play test with zero errors.

Playing it myself caught what the tests missed: getting stuck on the conveyor, freezing while holding an egg, walking through decorations and getting flung past obby levels. The game reached 463 visits. We shelved it on November 7 and took what we learned into our next game, +1 Speed Catch Animals.
projects.stack: Roblox Studio, Luau, Claude (AI coding agents), Game design

projects.title: HokieWallet
projects.role: Front-end lead, Team of four, VTHacks
projects.summary: A student finance dashboard prototype bringing budgets, spending, and campus wallet information into one view.
projects.detail: At VTHacks, I owned the front end of HokieWallet, a student finance prototype built by a team of four. I built the balance and budget screens in React and connected them to our Node.js back end. I also designed the color scheme, added support for 10 languages and accessibility settings, and tuned front-end performance. I set up our GitHub collaboration so all four of us could share and merge code. It is a prototype with sample data; it does not connect to real bank or university payment accounts.

projects.title: TopSecret
projects.role: Roles, web login and the first database layer, on a team of four
projects.summary: A team Java app that grew from a command-line tool into a web app with logins, roles, an audit log and a SQLite database. I built the roles, the web login and the first database layer.
projects.detail:
TopSecret was the semester project in Software Development Essentials at the University of Virginia in spring 2026. Four of us built one Java app across five assignments, and for each one we split the work into four parts. It started as a command-line tool that deciphered text files. It ended as a web app with logins, roles, an audit log and a SQLite database. I made 47 of the team's 132 commits.

- February | Command line | I wrote the entry point: argument parsing, input checks and a plain error message for every bad input, from a file number that isn't a number to a missing key file.
- March | Database | I moved storage from text files to SQLite. I wrote the connection manager and the mission repository, including the import that loads mission briefs from a TSV file.
- March | Roles | I built access levels. The first account to register becomes the admin and every later one starts as a standard user. Admins can promote and demote other users but never themselves, and each change is written to the audit log. Standard users never see the admin menu.
- April | Web login | I added a web mode on Java's built-in HTTP server: the login form, the session manager and its cookie, protected routes and logout. I also wrote the HTML page builder the web pages are built on.
- April | Finishing | Shared page styling, agent search that also covers dates and notes, and mission links that persist in the database.

I tested what I built. The role rules have tests for self-promotion, self-demotion, callers who aren't admins and users who don't exist. The web login has integration tests that sign in over HTTP and check the session cookie, the protected routes and logout. The team finished with 433 JUnit tests.

The code lives in a private class repository, so there is no public link.

projects.title: Carlos OS Portfolio
projects.summary: A personal portfolio with a searchable project catalog and shareable project briefings.
projects.detail: This portfolio began as a Virginia Tech CS 2104 class project. I supplied the concept, visual direction, personal background, and project content, and used AI tools to assist with implementation and testing. The Flask application queries a SQLite project catalog, supports search and category filters, and creates bookmarkable briefings from selected projects. It is packaged with Docker, tested with Python, and now hosted publicly on Render.
